changes.reason: Use analytic s, p and d trial orbitals in place of the pseudopotential's diffuse s2/p2 PAOs. The p triplet built from them carries most of the hopping weight beyond r_c. The count is unchanged at 1+3+5 = 9.
Keep the frozen window at E_F+4 eV, as in attempt 5, so that only the projector source changes. frozen_capacity shows at most 6 frozen states, below the 9 functions.

diagnosis: The subspace is fine, and so is the untruncated model (eta_2 = 4.0 meV, every other check passes). What fails is the sparse criterion: once hoppings longer than r_c = 9.82 Å are cut, eta_2 rises to 48.7 meV. The truncation diagnostics show that the three p-like Wannier functions (spread 2.97 Å² each) carry about 88 % of the hopping weight beyond r_c. The s-like function (2.11 Å²) carries about 7 %. The five d functions are compact (about 0.6–0.7 Å²). In PDWF the p functions come from the pseudopotential's 'p2' orbital, a nearly empty 4p shell that is very diffuse in this USPP. validate_deck also notes that the projector list and the UPF differ in their l=1 orbitals. Five PDWF attempts have changed the projectability thresholds, the frozen window and the orbital subset, and eta_2 stayed between 48.7 and 49.3 meV whenever the s, p and d orbitals were kept. Dropping p made it much worse (830 meV), and raising dis_proj_min to 0.01 left the deck infeasible. That whole class of PDWF knobs is exhausted. The p and s radial parts are fixed by the pseudopotential's own orbitals, and PDWF cannot replace them. Switching to SMV with analytic s, p and d projectors keeps the same 9-function manifold but takes the source of the radial parts away from the pseudopotential. The frozen window stays at E_F+4 eV. No reference in the corpus resolved this check, and the frontier dataset rows for V compounds use 0.95–0.99 thresholds, which this run has already covered.
